phases.name: Explore
phases.summary: Prove it small before betting big

phases.name: Deliver
phases.summary: Build it, then release it carefully

phases.name: Run
phases.summary: Measure it and decide its future

stages.name: Frame
stages.purpose: Frame the problem, the outcome and today's baseline, screen the risk, and agree the rules of a small proof of concept before anyone builds anything.
stages.keyQuestion: Is this a problem worth testing with AI?

stages.name: Prove
stages.purpose: Run a time-boxed proof of concept on real data with capped users, then decide with evidence whether to scale, iterate, pivot, or stop.
stages.keyQuestion: Does it work, and is it worth scaling?

stages.name: Build
stages.purpose: Design and build the production version with evaluation running on every change, and put in place the controls the risk tier needs.
stages.keyQuestion: Is it ready for real users?

stages.name: Launch
stages.purpose: Release to a pilot cohort with support, training and live monitoring, prove it holds up, then expand.
stages.keyQuestion: Does it hold up with real users?

stages.name: Run
stages.purpose: Run it, watch quality, drift, cost and incidents, measure value, and decide every quarter whether to keep investing, fix it, or retire it.
stages.keyQuestion: Is it still working and worth it?

riskTiers.name: Low
riskTiers.description: Internal productivity assistance with a human always in the loop, non-sensitive data, and limited blast radius if the AI is wrong.
riskTiers.rigor: Core controls plus the PoC charter and the Proof gate.

riskTiers.name: Moderate
riskTiers.summary: Business-critical workflow or material business impact.
riskTiers.description: Supports a business-critical workflow, touches customer data, or influences outcomes with material business impact. A human remains accountable for the final action.
riskTiers.rigor: Adds a privacy screen, a PoC security check, human oversight validation, a security and privacy review, monitoring and rollback plans, and a quarterly risk review.

riskTiers.name: High
riskTiers.summary: Consequential decisions, sensitive data, high autonomy, or significant exposure.
riskTiers.description: Makes or heavily shapes consequential decisions, acts with autonomy, uses sensitive or regulated data, or carries safety, regulatory, or significant reputational exposure.
riskTiers.rigor: Adds autonomy boundaries, a red-team smoke test during the PoC, adversarial and bias testing, verified override controls, executive residual-risk acceptance, board approval before full rollout, and an annual independent review.

readinessDimensions.name: Business Value
readinessDimensions.description: Is the outcome defined, the value hypothesis credible, and value being measured?

readinessDimensions.name: Product Readiness
readinessDimensions.description: Is the problem, user experience, scope, and limitation story clear and agreed?

readinessDimensions.name: Technical Readiness
readinessDimensions.description: Is the solution feasible, built, integrated, versioned, and backed by suitable data?

readinessDimensions.name: AI Evaluation
readinessDimensions.description: Has the AI been evaluated against defined criteria, at the right scale, with results documented?

readinessDimensions.name: Risk & Governance
readinessDimensions.description: Are risks assessed, mitigated, reviewed, and residual risk explicitly accepted?

readinessDimensions.name: Operational Readiness
readinessDimensions.description: Are support, monitoring, incident management, and rollback ready?

readinessDimensions.name: Adoption Readiness
readinessDimensions.description: Are users identified, trained, bought in, and is adoption being measured?

roles.name: Executive Sponsor
roles.responsibilities: Owns the business case, removes obstacles, and accepts residual risk.

roles.name: Product Manager
roles.responsibilities: Orchestrates the lifecycle, owns scope, priorities, and gate readiness.

roles.name: Business Owner
roles.responsibilities: Owns the target workflow and accepts the solution through UAT.

roles.name: AI / Solution Architect
roles.responsibilities: Owns the solution design, model and pattern choices, and known limitations.

roles.name: Engineering
roles.responsibilities: Builds, integrates, versions, and hardens the solution.

roles.name: Data Owner
roles.responsibilities: Validates data quality, rights to use, and lineage of knowledge sources.

roles.name: UX / Research
roles.responsibilities: Researches users and designs the workflow, including review and override moments.

roles.name: Security
roles.responsibilities: Assesses security threats, prompt-injection exposure, and access controls.

roles.name: Privacy / Legal
roles.responsibilities: Reviews personal data use, consent, and legal obligations.

roles.name: QA / Evaluation
roles.responsibilities: Defines evaluation criteria, runs test suites, and reports results.

roles.name: Operations
roles.responsibilities: Prepares support, monitoring, incident response, and runbooks.

roles.name: Governance / Risk
roles.responsibilities: Runs risk reviews and ensures governance requirements are evidenced.

roles.name: Finance
roles.responsibilities: Validates the value hypothesis and measures realized value.

roles.name: Other / Unknown
roles.responsibilities: Stakeholder with an unclear but persistent interest.

evidenceTemplates.name: AI Opportunity Brief
evidenceTemplates.description: One page on the problem, the users, the outcome, today's baseline, and why AI.

evidenceTemplates.name: Risk Screen
evidenceTemplates.description: Initial risk tier with its rationale and the first risks to watch.

evidenceTemplates.name: Privacy Screening
evidenceTemplates.description: Early screen for personal data, consent, and legal constraints.

evidenceTemplates.name: Golden Set and Eval Plan
evidenceTemplates.description: The golden cases, how answers are scored, and the pass thresholds.

evidenceTemplates.name: PoC Demo
evidenceTemplates.description: A recorded run of the proof of concept on approved sample data.

evidenceTemplates.name: PoC Eval Results
evidenceTemplates.description: Pass rate on the golden set against the charter threshold, with failure examples.

evidenceTemplates.name: Value Signal Report
evidenceTemplates.description: Measured effect on the key metric versus the baseline, from pilot users or a replay.

evidenceTemplates.name: Unit Economics
evidenceTemplates.description: Cost per task and projected annual run cost at full scale, against expected value.

evidenceTemplates.name: Data Assessment
evidenceTemplates.description: Production data sources, quality, access rights, sensitivity, and gaps.

evidenceTemplates.name: Scale Recommendation
evidenceTemplates.description: Scale, iterate, pivot or stop, with the build plan, team, and budget ask.

evidenceTemplates.name: Red-Team Smoke Test
evidenceTemplates.description: A short misuse and failure probe of the PoC before any build money is spent.

evidenceTemplates.name: Autonomy & Decision Boundaries
evidenceTemplates.description: What the AI may do on its own, what needs a human, and the hard limits.

evidenceTemplates.name: Solution Design
evidenceTemplates.description: Architecture, model and pattern choices, data flow, and where humans review or override.

evidenceTemplates.name: Working Solution and Version Record
evidenceTemplates.description: A recorded end-to-end demo plus the model, prompt, retrieval, and parameter versions in use.

evidenceTemplates.name: Evaluation Results
evidenceTemplates.description: Results of the eval suite against its thresholds, run on every change.

evidenceTemplates.name: Known Limitations
evidenceTemplates.description: Documented failure modes and where the solution should not be used.

evidenceTemplates.name: UAT Sign-off
evidenceTemplates.description: The business owner's acceptance for release to real users.

evidenceTemplates.name: Risk Review
evidenceTemplates.description: Pre-release review of the risk register and its mitigations.

evidenceTemplates.name: Human Oversight Validation
evidenceTemplates.description: Evidence that people can review, correct, and override AI output under real workload.

evidenceTemplates.name: Security & Privacy Review
evidenceTemplates.description: Security assessment, prompt-injection testing, and privacy impact review.

evidenceTemplates.name: Monitoring Plan
evidenceTemplates.description: What will be watched in production, alert thresholds, owners, and how to roll back.

evidenceTemplates.name: Adversarial Test Report
evidenceTemplates.description: Red-team, bias, and misuse findings and fixes.

evidenceTemplates.name: Override Controls Verification
evidenceTemplates.description: Proof that review, override, and kill-switch controls work as designed.

evidenceTemplates.name: Residual Risk Acceptance
evidenceTemplates.description: The executive sponsor's explicit acceptance of the remaining risk.

evidenceTemplates.name: Support Runbook
evidenceTemplates.description: Support model, escalation paths, and known-issue handling.

evidenceTemplates.name: Training & Comms Plan
evidenceTemplates.description: Training materials, communications, and rollout messaging.

evidenceTemplates.name: Monitoring Dashboard
evidenceTemplates.description: Live production monitoring with alerting switched on.

evidenceTemplates.name: Pilot Results
evidenceTemplates.description: Pilot cohort results against the eval bar and the adoption target.

evidenceTemplates.name: Rollout & Rollback Plan
evidenceTemplates.description: Who gets it when, and how to switch it off safely.

evidenceTemplates.name: Governance Board Approval
evidenceTemplates.description: AI governance board approval for full rollout of a high-risk solution.

evidenceTemplates.name: Monitoring Report
evidenceTemplates.description: Periodic production quality, drift, cost, and incident report.

evidenceTemplates.name: Periodic Evaluation Report
evidenceTemplates.description: Scheduled re-evaluation, and re-evaluation after any model change.

evidenceTemplates.name: Value Realization Report
evidenceTemplates.description: Realized value and adoption versus the value hypothesis.

evidenceTemplates.name: Independent Review
evidenceTemplates.description: Annual review by someone outside the team of a high-risk solution in production.

activityTemplates.name: Frame the problem and outcome
activityTemplates.description: Describe the problem in today's workflow, who it affects, and the measurable outcome you want.
activityTemplates.why: A clear problem and a measurable outcome keep the team from building a solution in search of a problem.
activityTemplates.consequence: Effort goes into a capability nobody asked for.

activityTemplates.name: Capture today's baseline
activityTemplates.description: Measure how the workflow performs today on the metric you want to move.
activityTemplates.why: You can't prove an improvement without knowing where you started.
activityTemplates.consequence: The PoC's value signal has nothing to compare against.

activityTemplates.name: Explain why AI beats simpler options
activityTemplates.description: Say why AI is a better fit than rules, a process change, or existing tools.
activityTemplates.why: Prevents using AI where simpler, cheaper, more reliable options exist.
activityTemplates.consequence: Unneeded complexity and cost.

activityTemplates.name: Screen the risk tier
activityTemplates.description: Set the initial risk tier with a short rationale and list the first risks to watch.
activityTemplates.why: The risk tier decides how much rigor every later stage needs.
activityTemplates.consequence: Controls are too heavy for a small idea, or too light for a risky one.

activityTemplates.name: Check that usable data exists
activityTemplates.description: Confirm a sample of the data the PoC needs exists and can be used for a test.
activityTemplates.why: No data, no proof. Finding out now costs a day; finding out in Build costs a quarter.
activityTemplates.consequence: The PoC stalls waiting for data.

activityTemplates.name: Screen privacy and legal constraints
activityTemplates.description: Check early for personal data, consent, and legal limits on the data and the use.
activityTemplates.why: Privacy issues found late can force a redesign or kill a project.
activityTemplates.consequence: Late-stage redesign or legal exposure.

activityTemplates.name: Draft autonomy boundaries
activityTemplates.description: Sketch what the AI may do on its own and what always needs a person.
activityTemplates.why: Autonomy is the biggest driver of consequence; draw the line before testing it.
activityTemplates.consequence: The PoC tests a level of autonomy nobody would approve.

activityTemplates.name: Compare build, buy, and partner options
activityTemplates.description: Check whether a vendor or platform already does this well enough.
activityTemplates.why: Avoids rebuilding commodity capability.
activityTemplates.consequence: Possible overspend.

activityTemplates.name: Build the golden eval set
activityTemplates.description: Collect real cases with known good answers and agree how answers are scored.
activityTemplates.why: Writing the eval before the build is what makes the PoC result believable.
activityTemplates.consequence: Success gets defined after the fact, and every PoC seems to work.

activityTemplates.name: Build the PoC on sample data
activityTemplates.description: Build the smallest version that can answer the hypothesis, on approved sample data, with no production writes.
activityTemplates.why: A sandboxed PoC tests the idea without risking real systems or customers.
activityTemplates.consequence: Too much is built before anyone knows it works.

activityTemplates.name: Run the eval and record results
activityTemplates.description: Run the PoC against the golden set and record the pass rate and failure examples.
activityTemplates.why: This is the quality half of the Proof gate.
activityTemplates.consequence: Scale decisions rest on demos instead of measured quality.

activityTemplates.name: Measure the value signal
activityTemplates.description: Measure the effect on the key metric with capped pilot users or a replay of real work.
activityTemplates.why: A model that works but saves nothing is not worth scaling.
activityTemplates.consequence: Build money goes to something that won't pay back.

activityTemplates.name: Estimate the cost to run at scale
activityTemplates.description: Estimate cost per task and annual run cost at full volume, including model and infrastructure costs.
activityTemplates.why: AI has a running cost per use; value minus run cost is the real return.
activityTemplates.consequence: A solution that costs more to run than it saves.

activityTemplates.name: Confirm production data access and rights
activityTemplates.description: Confirm the production data can be accessed, is good enough, and may be used this way.
activityTemplates.why: Sample data is easy; production data is where projects stall.
activityTemplates.consequence: Build starts and then waits months for data access.

activityTemplates.name: Write the scale recommendation
activityTemplates.description: Recommend scale, iterate, pivot, or stop, with the build plan, team, and budget ask.
activityTemplates.why: Gives the sponsor one clear recommendation to decide on.
activityTemplates.consequence: The Proof gate becomes a debate instead of a decision.

activityTemplates.name: Check PoC data handling with Security
activityTemplates.description: Confirm sample data, access, and the model provider setup are safe for a test.
activityTemplates.why: A PoC on real data is still a data exposure.
activityTemplates.consequence: Sensitive data leaks during a test.

activityTemplates.name: Run a red-team smoke test
activityTemplates.description: Spend a day trying to make the PoC fail or misbehave: misuse, bias, and prompt injection.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk failure modes should surface before build money is spent.
activityTemplates.consequence: Serious failure modes are found after the build.

activityTemplates.name: Define autonomy level and decision boundaries
activityTemplates.description: Agree, with evidence from the PoC, what the AI may do on its own and what needs a human.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI needs explicit, agreed limits before it is built for real.
activityTemplates.consequence: Autonomy creeps beyond what anyone approved.

activityTemplates.name: Design the solution and human oversight
activityTemplates.description: Decide the architecture, model and pattern, data flow, and where people review, approve, or override.
activityTemplates.why: Oversight designed in from the start works; oversight bolted on later gets skipped.
activityTemplates.consequence: Rework late in the build, or weak human control.

activityTemplates.name: Build the production version
activityTemplates.description: Build and integrate the production version, recording the model, prompt, and config versions in use.
activityTemplates.why: Versioned configuration is how you know what changed when quality moves.
activityTemplates.consequence: Nobody can explain why answers changed.

activityTemplates.name: Run the eval suite on every change
activityTemplates.description: Grow the golden set into an eval suite and run it on every model, prompt, or data change.
activityTemplates.why: AI quality moves with every change; continuous evaluation catches regressions early.
activityTemplates.consequence: A small change quietly makes answers worse.

activityTemplates.name: Document known limitations
activityTemplates.description: Write down known failure modes and where the solution should not be used.
activityTemplates.why: Users and supporters need to know where not to trust it.
activityTemplates.consequence: Misuse in situations it can't handle.

activityTemplates.name: Complete UAT
activityTemplates.description: The business tests the solution in realistic scenarios and signs off.
activityTemplates.why: The business must accept the solution before real users see it.
activityTemplates.consequence: A release the business doesn't trust.

activityTemplates.name: Review risks before release
activityTemplates.description: Review the risk register and confirm every serious risk has a working mitigation.
activityTemplates.why: Confirms mitigations are real and not just written down.
activityTemplates.consequence: Known risks reach users unmitigated.

activityTemplates.name: Validate human oversight in practice
activityTemplates.description: Show that people can review, correct, and override AI output under real workload.
activityTemplates.why: Oversight that works on paper often fails under real workload.
activityTemplates.consequence: Automation bias lets errors through unreviewed.

activityTemplates.name: Complete security and privacy review
activityTemplates.description: Assess security threats, prompt injection, access controls, and personal data handling.
activityTemplates.why: AI adds new attack surfaces and new ways to mishandle data.
activityTemplates.consequence: Security or privacy incidents after release.

activityTemplates.name: Define production monitoring plan
activityTemplates.description: Decide what to watch in production, the alert thresholds, the owners, and how to roll back.
activityTemplates.why: AI quality drifts. You need to know before your users do.
activityTemplates.consequence: Silent degradation in production.

activityTemplates.name: Run adversarial and bias testing
activityTemplates.description: Red-team the production version for misuse, bias, and prompt injection.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI must be stress-tested before real people depend on it.
activityTemplates.consequence: Harmful or unfair outcomes in production.

activityTemplates.name: Verify override and kill-switch controls
activityTemplates.description: Prove that review, override, and kill-switch controls work as designed.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI needs a proven way for people to stop it.
activityTemplates.consequence: No way to stop a misbehaving system quickly.

activityTemplates.name: Obtain executive residual-risk acceptance
activityTemplates.description: The executive sponsor explicitly accepts the risk that remains after mitigation.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI needs a named leader who accepts what is left.
activityTemplates.consequence: Nobody is accountable for the remaining risk.

activityTemplates.name: Integrate with target systems
activityTemplates.description: Connect to the systems people already work in.
activityTemplates.why: AI outside the workflow doesn't get used.
activityTemplates.consequence: Low adoption.

activityTemplates.name: Performance and load testing
activityTemplates.description: Test latency and throughput at expected production volume.
activityTemplates.why: Slow AI is abandoned AI.
activityTemplates.consequence: Poor experience at scale.

activityTemplates.name: Release to a pilot cohort
activityTemplates.description: Release to a small, named group of users first and expand on evidence.
activityTemplates.why: A pilot limits the blast radius while real-world performance is proven.
activityTemplates.consequence: Everyone is exposed to undiscovered issues at once.

activityTemplates.name: Stand up support and the runbook
activityTemplates.description: Set up the support model, escalation paths, and known-issue handling.
activityTemplates.why: Users need somewhere to go when the AI is wrong.
activityTemplates.consequence: Issues pile up with no owner.

activityTemplates.name: Deliver training and communications
activityTemplates.description: Train users on how to use it, and when not to trust it.
activityTemplates.why: Trained users get more value and catch more errors.
activityTemplates.consequence: Low adoption and misuse.

activityTemplates.name: Turn on live monitoring and alerts
activityTemplates.description: Switch on production monitoring for quality, drift, cost, and incidents, with alerts.
activityTemplates.why: You can't manage what you can't see.
activityTemplates.consequence: Problems are found by users first.

activityTemplates.name: Compare pilot results to the eval bar
activityTemplates.description: Measure accuracy, overrides, escalations, and adoption on real traffic against the targets.
activityTemplates.why: Offline evaluation never fully predicts production behavior.
activityTemplates.consequence: Full rollout proceeds on lab results alone.

activityTemplates.name: Plan the phased rollout and rollback
activityTemplates.description: Decide who gets it when, and how to switch it off safely if needed.
activityTemplates.why: A planned rollout with a tested way back keeps surprises small.
activityTemplates.consequence: No safe way back when something goes wrong.

activityTemplates.name: Get governance board approval for full rollout
activityTemplates.description: Present pilot evidence and residual risk to the AI governance board.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI needs board-level approval before everyone depends on it.
activityTemplates.consequence: High-risk AI scales without oversight.

activityTemplates.name: Monitor quality, drift, cost, and incidents
activityTemplates.description: Review production quality, drift, run cost, and incidents on a regular cadence.
activityTemplates.why: AI degrades quietly; regular review catches it.
activityTemplates.consequence: Silent quality loss and cost creep.

activityTemplates.name: Re-evaluate on schedule and after model changes
activityTemplates.description: Re-run the eval suite on a schedule and after every model, prompt, or data change.
activityTemplates.why: Model providers update and retire models; every change can move quality.
activityTemplates.consequence: A model update silently lowers quality.

activityTemplates.name: Measure adoption and realized value
activityTemplates.description: Measure usage and realized value against the value hypothesis.
activityTemplates.why: Value is the reason it exists; measure it like revenue.
activityTemplates.consequence: Nobody knows if it paid off.

activityTemplates.name: Quarterly risk review
activityTemplates.description: Review the risk register, incidents, and any changes since the last review.
activityTemplates.why: Risk changes as usage, data, and models change.
activityTemplates.consequence: Stale controls on a changing system.

activityTemplates.name: Annual independent review
activityTemplates.description: Someone outside the team reviews the solution, its controls, and its outcomes.
activityTemplates.why: High-risk AI needs a fresh pair of eyes at least once a year.
activityTemplates.consequence: Blind spots persist.

activityTemplates.name: Collect user feedback
activityTemplates.description: Gather what users like, dislike, and need next.
activityTemplates.why: Feedback drives the next round of improvements.
activityTemplates.consequence: Improvements miss what users need.

gates.name: Commit to a test
gates.question: Is this worth testing?
gates.description: Confirms the problem is real, the outcome is measurable, the risk is screened, and the PoC's rules are agreed before it starts.

criteria.label: Problem statement documented
criteria.description: At least a sentence describing the problem in today's workflow.

criteria.label: Target users defined
criteria.description: Who uses or is affected by the solution.

criteria.label: Business outcome defined
criteria.description: A measurable outcome, not a feature.

criteria.label: PoC charter agreed
criteria.description: A hypothesis, a timebox, a budget cap, and pass thresholds set before the PoC starts.

gates.name: Proof gate
gates.question: Does it work, and is it worth scaling?
gates.description: Nothing gets build money until a time-boxed proof on real data clears the thresholds in its charter. Scale, iterate, pivot, or stop.

criteria.label: Quality meets the charter
criteria.description: Pass rate on the golden eval set meets the charter threshold.

criteria.label: Value signal meets the charter
criteria.description: Measured improvement against the baseline meets the charter target.

criteria.label: Run cost within the ceiling
criteria.description: Projected annual run cost stays under the charter's share of expected value.

criteria.label: No unmitigated high or critical risks
criteria.description: Every open high or critical risk has a mitigation and an owner.

gates.name: Release readiness
gates.question: Is it ready for real users?
gates.description: Confirms a production-grade version exists, its evaluation holds, and the controls its risk tier needs are in place. Decided by someone outside the build team.

criteria.label: Success metrics have baselines and targets
criteria.description: At least two metrics with a baseline and a target.

criteria.label: No unmitigated high or critical risks
criteria.description: Every open high or critical risk has a mitigation and an owner.

gates.name: Scale-out
gates.question: Does it hold up with real users?
gates.description: Confirms the pilot met its bar, people are using it, and support is in place before everyone gets it.

criteria.label: Pilot results measured
criteria.description: At least two metrics with current values from the pilot.

gates.name: Quarterly value review
gates.question: Is it still working and worth it?
gates.description: A recurring review rather than an exit: keep investing, fix what slipped, or retire it responsibly.
